A frequent frustration is that two evaluators can score the same call very differently, or that agents get marked down for things outside their control. Qualtrics research found about a third of agents felt their performance wasn't fairly evaluated. The fixes are standardized rubrics applied to every call, regular calibration sessions among evaluators, an appeals process for agents, and automated scoring that applies identical criteria consistently rather than relying on one reviewer's [...] However, teams that rely solely on manual QA processes will run into one big issue: They’re only able to evaluate 1–2% of calls, which inevitably leads to gaps in coaching and customer experience data (more on this below).

This one problem leads to issues such as agents getting frustrated during coaching sessions because they’re being coached on one-off mistakes, or missing certain customer complaints because they never came up in the calls that were reviewed. [...] How many calls should actually be scored for call center QA?

Traditional manual QA typically evaluates only about 2–5 calls per agent per week, which works out to roughly 1–2% of total volume. The common complaint is that this tiny sample isn't representative and lets both great and poor calls go unseen. The modern best practice is to use automated quality assurance software to score close to 100% of interactions, then route the flagged outliers to humans for deeper review.

hits.title: Call Centre Quality Assurance: Everything You Need to Know
hits.snippet:
If your call centre’s quality assurance programme is being done manually, it’s often impossible to vet and monitor every call handled by every agent. Instead, you’ll likely take a representative sample at various points and track those against your chosen goals. The goal here would be to look for coachable moments and find areas where agents can improve. You might also rely on post-call surveys that solicit feedback from customers.

### Automated (unsampled) call centre QA [...] In this article we’re going to focus on call centre quality assurance in particular – the what, why, and how. In that setting, quality assurance refers to the act of monitoring every customer interaction your contact centre has, and using a defined process to improve the customer experience. [...] In general, call centre quality assurance is all about tightening the various nuts and bolts of your contact centre, fine-tuning agent performance, and delivering more positive customer interactions.
